div.p: Distributed safety-critical real-time systems are required to be real-time and reliable. By the use of CSMA/CD mechanism, Ethernet is not suitable to provide real-time and reliable service. To solve this problem, this paper presents a hard real-time communication protocol based on shared Ethernet and which can provides schedulability analysis and on-line scheduling based on TDMA mechanism with master/slave scheme. And it is oriented to message, guarantees hard real-time communication. This protocol schedules not only the transmission of the messages but also the production of the messages, and supports dynamic changes in the communication requirements.
This protocol resolves the unpredictability problem of Ethernet communication, in order to improve the real-time and reliability of the system, which doesn't modify the hardware of Ethernet.

div.head: Introduction 1
div.p: Distributed safety-critical real-time systems need the support of reliable and real-time communication network. But by the use of CSMA/CD mechanism, Ethernet is not suitable to provide time-bounded and reliable service. Several approaches and techniques have been used to make Ethernet deterministic so as to take advantage of its low cost and higher speeds. Some of these approaches are MAC modification, token passing, TDMA, switched Ethernet and so on.

However, these protocols either require specialized hardware, or provide probabilistic timeliness guarantee, or require complicated algorithm for time-Financial supports from the AMD & SUN University program 200702 triggered tasks scheduling, or provide low efficiency, or are lack of the mechanism that permits on-line node addition and removal as well as messages streams addition and removal. To solve the above problems, the paper presents a new protocol for hard real-time communication based on shared Ethernet.

div.head: Hard real-time communication
div.p: Among all of the approaches improving real-time performance on the shared Ethernet, the TDMA mechanism with master/slave scheme which is called FTT [7] ,has higher efficiency and flexibility. Similarly to E&TTE [1] ,FTT-Ethernet [2] and WorldFIP [8] , the new protocol proposed in this paper, uses the FTT method.

div.head: Architecture
div.p: The new protocol proposed in this paper, similarly to E&TTE [1] , FTT-Ethernet [2] and WorldFIP [8] , uses the key concept of Elementary Cycle(EC). The bus time consists of successive Elementary Cycles. EC has the fixed length. As shown in Figure 1 and Figure 2, there are three windows within each EC. They are SYN window, CSMA/CD window, and TDMA window。 Figure 1. Elementary Cycle (1)SYN window At the beginning of the SYN window, the SYN frame is broadcasted by the master. The SYN frame includes the production information, the transmission information, the acknowledgements of the addition requests of the new nodes, and the current system state. After receiving and searching the SYN frame, each slave begins to set up the transmission timers and produce the frames of the messages by calling the relative production procedures. The acknowledgements inserted in the SYN frame show that the node addition requests are or not admitted by the scheduling algorithm.

(2)CSMA/CD window In the CSMA/CD window, slave nodes are permitted to send non-real-time traffic, and new nodes of the network send the node addition requests to the master. Within this window, Carrier Sense Multiple Access with Collision Detection mechanism is used to solve the concurrent access to the shared Ethernet.

(3)TDMA window Within the TDMA window, slave nodes access the shared Ethernet using TDMA mechanism, and transmit real-time traffic at the pre-defined instants. And the non-periodic messages are transmitted in the subwindow Aperiodic, and the periodic messages are transmitted in the sub-window Periodic. The periodic messages which are transmitted but not produced within this EC, are arranged in the <Tx only> area, and periodic messages which are both transmitted and produced within this EC, are arranged in the <Pr&Tx> area.

div.head: Main Operations
div.p: There are two main operations in this protocol.

(1)Node and Stream addition and removal During the CSMA/CD window, nodes of the network which are off-line, transmit the node addition requests to the master. As shown in Figure 2, slave_2 sends a node addition request frame (NARF) within the CSMA/CD window. After receiving NARF, the master assigns a new identification to the node, updates NPT table and adds the information of message 0 of the new node into PMPT. The acknowledgement is inserted into the next SYN frame. With receiving the acknowledgement the new slave updates its local ID and on-line state.

Slave nodes use the frame of message 1 to report the requests of addition and removal of the messages to the master. With addition or removal of the periodic messages on the slaves, the salves update the frames of the message 1 using the properties of these messages. The flag which indicates addition or removal is also inserted into message 1 frame.
(2)Message Operations The properties of the periodic messages are put into PMT on the slaves. The slaves transmit periodic messages under the TDMA mechanism at the scheduled instants.

The non-periodic messages have two types. The non-periodic messages which have short deadline are converted into periodic messages. Their periods are set to half of the original ones. As for the non-periodic messages which have long deadlines, the slaves insert their properties into AMT table. For these messages, their traffic requirements are reported by periodic message 0. Message 0 is sent to report that there are non-periodic messages which wait for transmission. The master puts the non-periodic messages properties into MWFTT.
Nodes transmit non-real-time traffic within the CSMA/CD window, using CSMA/CD mechanism to access the shard Ethernet.

div.head: Schedulability Analysis
div.p: In this protocol, there are three phases in the scheduling mechanism. They are Collection of information, On-line Schedulability Test and On-line Scheduling respectively. There are some data structures used in this section, such as Periodic

div.head: Message Properties Table (PMPT), Messages Waiting for Transmission Table (MWFTT), and Nodes Properties Table (NPT)
div.p: . PMPT contains all of the periodic messages including the converted periodic messages on the network. MWFTT is consisted of the messages which are waiting for scheduling to be transmitted. And NPT includes the properties of the slave nodes, which are used to revise the production time. The production time is the execution time of the production procedure of the message, without any interrupt.

(1)Collection of Information Two types of the information are collected, the properties of the network nodes and the properties of the real-time messages. The master puts the node properties in the frames of node addition requests in NPT. Message 1 is used by the slave node to report the properties of periodic messages to the master, and these properties are put in the PMPT on the master. The presence of the non-periodic messages is reported to the master by message 0 of the slaves, and the properties of these non-periodic are put in MWFTT on the master.

(2) On-line Schedulability Test The schedulability test includes two phases: basic judgment and simulation judgment. In basic judgment phase, the real-time traffic on the bus must be less than λ 1 *EC(λ 1 <1). During simulation judgment phase, t is the least common multiple of all of the message periods in PMPT. From the first EC to the t EC, the scheduling algorithm on the master arranges as much the messages transmission as possible, within each EC. The message set is not schedulable, if there is a periodic message which is not arranged in any one of its period.

(3)On-line scheduling On-line scheduling is responsible for making sure the following information within each EC: which messages to be produced as well as the production order, which messages to be transmitted, and the transmission instants, the current system state and configuration, and the acknowledgements of the node addition requests.

div.head: Relationship between production and transmission
div.p: In other similar protocols, master schedules the transmission of the messages, while the slaves are responsible for scheduling the production of the messages. As shown in Figure 3(a), the message production completed by the slave is in front of the message period. And the master schedules the message to be transmitted within its period. It is possible that the difference between the transmission and the production is more than the message period, therefore the timeliness is not guaranteed. .

In the new protocol proposed in this paper, as shown in Figure 3(b), the master schedules both the production and the transmission of the message. And they are arranged in one of the message cycle. Therefore the difference between the transmission and the production of the message is less than the message period. The timeliness is guaranteed.

div.head: Figure 3. Production and Transmission
div.p: Other similar protocols use the time-triggered tasks to create periodic messages, and require complicated algorithm for time-triggered tasks scheduling. There's a possibility that some of the tasks have not been completed by their deadlines because of the preemption or other situations. It is possible that the message production has not been finished when the message is scheduled to be transmitted.

In the new protocol, which messages to be produced, as well as the production order, are scheduled by the master, within each EC. There is not complicated algorithm for the message productions scheduling. On the side, the scheduling mechanism makes sure that the transmission instants are later than the finish instants of the message productions.

Table I 4(a) shows the scheduling result according to the properties in Table I. Messages 1,2,3 are produced and messages 1,2 are transmitted during the EC0. But message 3 is not arranged to be transmitted within the EC0 for lack of the real-time bandwidth. And message 3 is scheduled to be transmitted within the EC1. During the EC3, message 1,3 are produced and transmitted. Because the finish instant of the production of the message 3 is later than that of message 1, the transmission instant of message 3 is later than that of message 1.

div.head: Conclusions
div.p: Distributed safety-critical real-time systems need the support of reliable and real-time communication network. Concerning the Shared Ethernet itself does not provide deterministic communication services, this paper proposed a new communication technique based on the traditional Ethernet. This technique converts the non-periodic real-time messages to periodic messages, directly or indirectly. The master node triggers the production of the time-triggered messages on the slaves regularly, and schedules the messages to be transmitted with no collisions.

In this new protocol, the productions of the periodic messages on the slaves are controlled by the master, so the messages created are predictable. The transmission time instants of the messages are calculated by the scheduling algorithm on the master in advance, therefore the transmission instants are predictable. Because of the predictability of the production and transmission of the messages, the system could never lose any of the real-time messages, and all messages could meet their deadlines. So the system has the ability to meet the time-bounded requirement, and make the transmission of the real-time messages reliable.
